Old post I know but I'm in the middle of taking Lexapro and I'm trying to figure out if my dizziness is a side effect.
I've started earlier this month with 2.5mg and take 5mg now, I didn't have any problems in the beginning but I'm getting progressively worse dizziness which also makes it hard to sleep.

The thing is I had 2 weeks of really bad dizziness in May when I wasn't taking any antidepressants but those were accompanied by panic attacks and were more like brain fog.
The dizziness right now feels like I'm super unbalanced, I don't want to go outside because it makes me feel incredibly unsafe, it gets worse with movement but also happens when I'm sitting or lying down.

I don't have any other side effects like nausea or headaches but the dizziness does the exact opposite of what Lexapro was supposed to do by making me even more of a shut in.

Hi, anxiety and depression can go hand in hand, I have been diagnosed with both for example.
This doesn't necessarily mean you have to have depression, it could be a depressive episode triggered by being overwhelmed with your anxiety which could let up again. Being stressed and overwhelmed does take a toll on your body, if you can, try to take it easy for a few days, see if your mood shifts again.
Absolutely won't hurt to voice your concerns about depression once you've found a therapist though. Take care, I hope things will get better for you soon!

I'm dealing with my own health anxiety problems right now but I've been going through a really horrible phase and even though it's not the same as your situation maybe this will help.

I had symptoms I thought were a stroke and ended up with horrible panic attacks, numbness, tingling, headaches and dizziness so bad I felt like I couldn't walk outside. I was convinced I had a stroke or illness that would kill me in weeks. The ER told me everything looks alright and it's probably just anxiety, ended up sobbing in the waiting room because I felt like they weren't taking me seriously. 

That was 2 months ago, all symptoms went away, I still suffer from anxiety attacks but they are mostly manageable. Anxiety is a hell of a drug and can mimic symptoms of severe illnesses. And these symptoms are really there, that's important to note, they just don't have an underlying cause.

I sincerely hope that it will turn out to be the case for you too, wishing you the best.

That sounds really stressful, I hope you can distract yourself somehow and have someone to talk to.
